dublinCore.title: FFT Butterfly
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Signal Processing
FFT
Algorithms
Butterfly Diagram
Bit-Reversal Permutation
dublinCore.description: Step-by-step diagram of the input reordering of a radix-2 decimation-in-time FFT: each step splits every group of samples into its even-indexed and odd-indexed halves until the samples sit in bit-reversed order, ready for the butterfly stages. FFT sizes 4, 8, 16 and 32.

learningObjectives: Describe one decimation-in-time step as splitting every group of samples into its even-indexed and odd-indexed halves
Calculate the number of columns (log2 N), the number of splits (log2 N - 1) and the group size after split s (N / 2^s) for a given FFT size
Predict the row that sample x[n] occupies in the final column by reversing the bits of n, and verify the prediction in the diagram
Explain why the final pairs x[m] and x[m + N/2] are the inputs of the first butterfly stage
Compare the (N/2) log2 N complex multiplications of the radix-2 FFT with the N^2 of the direct DFT
prerequisites: Definition of the DFT and its N^2 cost
Even and odd indices of a sequence

misconceptions.misconception: Bit-reversed order means the list is reversed
misconceptions.correction: The bits of each index are reversed, not the order of the list
misconceptions.evidence: For N = 8, x[0] and x[7] stay at the top and bottom while x[4] moves up to row 1

misconceptions.misconception: The right-hand column is the FFT output X[k]
misconceptions.correction: Reordering only moves the input samples; the butterfly stages that follow do the arithmetic
misconceptions.evidence: The green circles carry the same sample labels as the orange circles

accessibility.screenReaderScript: FFT butterfly reordering diagram. Columns of numbered circles show the input samples of a radix-2 FFT. Each press of Next Step splits every group into its even-indexed and odd-indexed samples and draws lines showing where each sample moves, ending in bit-reversed order. Radio buttons choose 4, 8, 16 or 32 points.

controls.label: Start / Next Step
controls.description: Adds the next column: splits every group into its even-indexed and odd-indexed samples and draws where each sample moves

controls.label: Reset
controls.description: Returns the diagram to the natural order (step 1)

controls.label: FFT Size
controls.description: Chooses the number of samples N (4, 8, 16 or 32) and resets the diagram

visualElements.description: Columns of sample nodes (orange natural order, light blue intermediate splits, green bit-reversed order) joined by navy lines that show where each sample moves; gray bars mark group boundaries
Binary sample indices beside the first and last columns, a step counter in the title, and a caption giving the number and size of the groups

model.description: Starting from the natural order 0..N-1, split s divides every group of N/2^(s-1) samples into its even-position and odd-position halves. After log2(N) - 1 splits the order is the bit-reversal permutation, the input order of an in-place radix-2 decimation-in-time FFT.
equations: groups after split s: 2^s groups of N / 2^s
complex multiplications: (N/2) log2 N versus N^2
limitations: Shows only the reordering of the inputs; the butterfly arithmetic and twiddle factors are not drawn
FFT sizes are limited to 4, 8, 16 and 32

instructionalStrategies: Predict-then-verify the final row of a sample by reversing its bits
Count splits and group sizes for each FFT size
Connect each split to the identity X[k] = E[k] + W_N^k O[k]
extensions: Add the butterfly stages with twiddle factors after the reordering
Show the decimation-in-frequency variant, where the outputs come out in bit-reversed order
